questions.question: Which precursor distinguishes near-critical quasi-static bursts from the distribution over the entire failure process?

options.A: The sampled-near-failure exponent crosses from −5/2 to −3/2
options.B: The whole-process exponent crosses from −3/2 to −1
options.C: Both distributions retain exponent −5/2 but differ only in normalization

questions.rationale: All bursts follow the universal −5/2 tail, while bursts sampled in the interval (0.9xc,xc) show −3/2.
questions.evidence_quote: the exponent of burst distribution shows a crossover from −5/2 to −3/2

questions.question: For uniform thresholds P(x)=x, how does the paper propose extrapolating the critical elongation from measurements of average burst size?

options.A: Plot Δav^(1/0.9) against x and extrapolate the fitted near-critical line to the x-axis
options.B: Plot Δav² against total force and take its maximum
options.C: Plot the inverse burst count against x and use its minimum
options.D: Fit Δav∝(xc−x)⁻⁵/² directly and identify xc from the y-intercept

questions.rationale: The reported average burst behavior is Δav≈(xc−x)^0.9, so the 1/0.9 power linearizes it.
questions.evidence_quote:
if we plot ∆1/0.9
av vs. x, we should get a straight line

questions.question: In the equal-step force-controlled case with uniform thresholds, what critical stress and susceptibility exponent follow from the fixed-point analysis?
questions.rationale: The fixed point gives U*=1/2±(σc−σ)^(1/2) with σc=1/4, and χ scales with exponent −1/2.

questions.question: How does the relaxation time behave as applied stress approaches σc from below in the paper's equal-step model?

options.A: τ∝(σc−σ)⁻¹/², the same divergence exponent magnitude as susceptibility
options.C: τ remains finite while susceptibility diverges

questions.rationale: The linearized recursion yields a diverging relaxation time with θ=1/2.

questions.question: For a slightly overloaded bundle σ=σc+ε, what relation links the breaking-rate minimum to the final collapse step?

options.A: tf=2t0, so the minimum occurs halfway to collapse
options.B: t0=2tf, so the minimum follows collapse
options.D: The minimum occurs at a fixed stress-independent step

questions.rationale: The recursion solution gives the minimum at half the total step count.

questions.question: How are energy emissions assigned to a burst of Δ failed fibers under the model's unit force constant?

options.A: En=½KΣ from i=min to Δ+min of xi², summing the squared thresholds of the failing fibers
options.B: En=KΔ times the bundle's total force at failure
options.C: En=½Kx² for the weakest fiber only, regardless of burst size

questions.rationale: The burst energy sums the elastic energy released by each failing fiber at its own threshold.
questions.evidence_quote:

ergy of amount 1
2Kx2 will be released

questions.question: What contrast does the paper report for energy-burst exponents below and above critical stress?

options.A: Below critical the exponent is −1, while above critical it is −1.5
options.B: Below critical it is −1.5, while above critical it is −1
options.D: Below critical is exponential and above critical follows −3/2

questions.rationale: The reported below- and above-critical energy distributions differ in their power-law slopes.

questions.question: Which assumption makes the reported results directly testable in a single simulated system rather than requiring rare-event aggregation?

options.A: The authors choose a large single bundle and uniform thresholds on [0,1] to expose precursors in one sample
options.B: They average over infinitely many independent bundles with Gaussian thresholds
options.C: They restrict analysis to the weakest fiber in each of many small bundles
options.D: They infer precursors only from laboratory acoustic emissions

questions.rationale: The study explicitly aims to observe precursors within a single large bundle and uses P(x)=x.

questions.question: What is the stated domain limitation of the crossover signature as a failure predictor?

options.A: It warns that failure is imminent but does not by itself give the critical elongation; the average-burst plot is used for that estimate
options.B: It gives the exact collapse time but not the critical stress
options.C: It applies only after total collapse and therefore cannot warn in advance
options.D: It cannot be observed in a single bundle

questions.rationale: The authors distinguish a warning signature from predicting xc quantitatively with average burst size.
questions.evidence_quote: the crossover signature can only warn of an imminent failure

questions.question: What modeling restriction most directly limits how broadly the paper's precursor exponents can be generalized?

options.A: The analysis fixes equal load sharing and illustrates results using uniformly distributed thresholds
options.B: It considers only a finite element mesh with spatially varying elasticity
options.C: It uses Gaussian thresholds and local load redistribution only
options.D: It studies experimental composites with unknown fiber-level thresholds

questions.rationale: The main numerical illustration assumes uniform thresholds and the model throughout is equal-load-sharing, so universality is conditional on the model class.
questions.evidence_quote: we consider the uniform distribution of fiber thresholds: P(x) = x
